strings.Decode only, no reload, also in the midd: Decode only, no reload, also in the middle of an answer (the engine switches between two tokens). The decode cores chosen above are the MINIMUM: a model opens with them and Auto adds cores on top. It follows Android's own throttling signals: the thermal headroom (100 % = the device throttles hard) and the thermal status. While the headroom is below 90 % and the throttle step is at most 1 (light), one more core, the fastest one not in use, is added; the decode speed over the next about 100 tokens decides: slower than before, it is taken back and Auto waits 5 minutes before the next try. From 95 % headroom an added core goes again. When the device really throttles (status moderate or worse, or Honor's own step 3), the added cores go first and Auto waits 5 minutes before adding again; if it still throttles, Auto goes below the chosen cores (never below 2); they come back when it stops. The title bar shows the headroom ("heat") and the cores in use.
strings.Decode writes the answer one token at a: Decode writes the answer one token at a time (this sets the t/s), prefill reads your message before the answer

strings.The model opens with the cache above. Wh: The model opens with the cache above. While more than the reserve below (plus the headroom) is free and none of the app lands in zram, the cache grows in steps (once it is full; step and pace are set below). When free RAM falls under the reserve or the app's zram grows, it shrinks again, also during an answer, never under the cache above. Everything it grew by is offered to Android: starting another app makes the system drop that part at once instead of compressing or closing apps.

strings.These five apply at once, no reload. Fas: These five apply at once, no reload. Faster growth (small step, short pace, low headroom) follows free RAM closely but moves memory more often; slower growth is calmer. A shrink takes back at least the amount above, more if free RAM is further under the reserve. The pause keeps the cache from growing right back into the pressure. The sampling pace is 2 s, so nothing reacts faster than that.
strings.These options apply only when the APK in: These options apply only when the APK includes the Hexagon backend. Prompt prefill can use the NPU; token-by-token decode remains on CPU.
strings.This setting uses native Android UI comp: This setting uses native Android UI components only. It does not generate or execute HTML/CSS/JavaScript. Interactive Artifacts are a separate feature for standalone HTML, SVG or Mermaid previews.
strings.This share of the cache, the experts unu: This share of the cache, the experts unused the longest, is offered to Android (MADV_FREE). The app does not decide when: the kernel takes offered pages when free RAM falls under its own thresholds, before it compresses anything into zram or closes an app, and for free. A dropped expert is read from flash again when needed. The rest is ordinary memory: Android can only move it into zram. The cache shrinks with what the kernel takes and grows back once it stops, but never under the share that is not offered. With Auto the share counts on the minimum; what Auto grew by is always offered. Off = ordinary memory.
